drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Here is your opening item. A platform team runs Claude Code in a nightly job.
drills.answer_line: SAM: The answer is B. The alias moved to a newer model
drills.stem: A nightly Claude Code job uses the sonnet alias in project settings. One morning its summaries change structure, though nobody changed code, prompts or settings. The team wants model upgrades only when they choose. What should they do?

options.A: Add a CLAUDE.md line telling Claude to keep the old structure
options.B: Set a full model name in project settings; move to a newer model only after evals pass
options.C: Switch the alias to opus so the job always runs the most capable model
options.D: Run each night's job with --continue so it sees the previous night's output

drills.why: Aliases move to newer versions. A full model name stops the drift, and evals decide when to move. A is guidance aimed at a version problem.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A developer wants Claude to use their own sandbox U R L
drills.answer_line: ALEX: C. A reaches every teammate.
drills.stem: A developer wants Claude to use their own sandbox URL and test account in one repository. Teammates must not get these instructions, and they should not apply in other projects. Where should they go?

options.C: CLAUDE.local.md at the project root, kept out of git
options.D: A .claude/rules file with a paths field

drills.why: CLAUDE.local.md is personal, one project, never committed. A reaches teammates, B reaches every project, D is committed and scopes by file.

drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.prompt: True or false: (1) an @ import lowers context cost because the file loads only when needed; (2) a rules file with a paths field loads only for matching files; (3) a deny rule still blocks in bypass permissions mode; (4) home-directory settings override the project's committed settings.json.
drills.answer: 1 false (imports load at launch); 2 true; 3 true; 4 false (user settings sit below project settings).

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A team's review subagent should build up knowledge
drills.answer_line: ALEX: A. B is mine alone
drills.stem: A review subagent should build up knowledge of this repository's recurring defects across sessions, and teammates should benefit through version control. What should the team configure?

options.A: The subagent's memory field set to project
options.B: The subagent's memory field set to user
options.C: A CLAUDE.md line telling the subagent to remember what it finds
options.D: Rely on the main session's auto memory

drills.why: Project-scope agent memory lives in the repo's .claude folder and can be version-controlled. User scope is personal; auto memory is machine-local.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A nightly pipeline must run Claude Code
drills.answer_line: SAM: A and B. C needs a person
drills.stem: Choose two. A nightly pipeline must run Claude Code with no one watching, and a script must read the final result and the session ID so a later step can resume it. Which two?

options.C: Start an interactive session and copy the result into a file
options.D: Add a CLAUDE.md line asking Claude to print its answer as JSON

drills.why: -p runs non-interactively; json output carries the result and session ID. D is a request for what the flag already gives; E returns nothing.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A developer on their own laptop is running a long refactor
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is a classic distractor
drills.stem: On their own laptop, a developer running a long refactor is tired of approving every shell command. They want Claude to keep working while something still blocks risky actions like force pushes and production deploys. Which permission mode fits?
drills.why: Auto mode puts a classifier in front of risky actions. Bypass removes safety checks and belongs in isolated containers; acceptEdits still prompts; dontAsk denies.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments, and the two questions under all of them.
drills.answer_line: ALEX: The CLAUDE dot md hierarchy and rules, settings and pinning
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the two questions under all of them.
drills.answer: CLAUDE.md hierarchy and rules; settings, pinning and plugins; skills, commands and agents; sessions, headless and auto mode. Who does it reach, and when does it load?

In this episode: Place an instruction at the right CLAUDE.md level
Pin a model so upgrades happen when you choose
Skill, command or subagent, and memory that lasts
Run unattended: headless, streaming, permission modes
Cold open: the overnight change: About four items on a 53-item paper
The CLAUDE.md hierarchy and rules: Files concatenate; subdirectory files load on first use
CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration
@ imports organise, up to 4 hops, load at launch
.claude/rules/ with a paths glob loads only for matching files
/init writes a starter CLAUDE.md; /memory opens memory files
Settings, pinning and plugins: Order: managed, command line, local, project, user
Permission rules: allow, ask, deny; lists merge across scopes
Aliases opus, sonnet, haiku resolve to newer versions over time
On the API, a model ID is a pinned snapshot
Version prompts beside the model they were tested on
Plugins: namespaced, version field, dependencies list
Skills, commands and agents: A skill's description lets Claude load it when relevant
disable-model-invocation: only a person starts it
Subagents: fresh context, own prompt and tools, only the result returns
Auto memory: per repo, machine-local, MEMORY.md index
Subagent memory field: user, project or local scope
Sessions, headless and auto mode: --continue for the latest session; --resume with a session ID
Headless runs for scripts and pipelines
Output formats for final results and live events
Permission modes, from ask-first to skip-all
Cold open: the verdict: The alias moved to a newer model
Pin a full model name; evals decide when to move
A CLAUDE.md line gives no control over the next release
Tell: "only when they choose" and "nobody changed anything"
Five to remember: CLAUDE.md levels concatenate; CLAUDE.local.md is personal and uncommitted
Imports load at launch; a paths glob loads only on matching files
Settings order managed to user; deny holds; "must never" needs settings or a hook
Aliases move: pin, version prompts with the model, gate with evals
Side-effect skills: disable-model-invocation; unattended: -p; fewer prompts, safety checks: auto
Recap: the exam tells: "Must never", "every time" → deny rule or hook
One file type across the tree → rules file with a paths glob
Changed with no change of yours → moving alias; pin
Settings disagree → higher level wins; deny always holds
Agent should learn and share → memory: project
Unattended → -p with json; fewer prompts, risks blocked → auto
